os_version: 6.10 (Final), userland of the PyPA image quay.io/pypa/manylinux2010_x86_64 (glibc 2.12)
environment_detail: A DOCKER CONTAINER, NOT A CENTOS 6 MACHINE. The lowest testable Linux system of the project (PoC scope rule of 2026-11-15, spec Clarifications: manylinux2010, glibc 2.12, in Docker; success here counts for newer systems; no other distribution, no i686, no ARM). The userland is the PyPA image quay.io/pypa/manylinux2010_x86_64 (digest sha256:3b5eb5ab9bc73b93740ae4eda9962078951cd3bb7efe837b770360e78c7366fb, created 2022-08-05) with the packages of tools/trials/linux-manylinux2010-x86_64/Dockerfile added: CentOS release 6.10 (Final), glibc 2.12-1.212.1.el6_10.3, libstdc++ 4.4.7-23.el6 (GLIBCXX_3.4.13 at most), libX11 1.6.4-4.el6_10, libXft 2.3.2-1.el6, fontconfig 2.8.0-5.el6, freetype 2.3.11-19.el6_10, xorg-x11-server-Xvfb 1.17.4-18.el6.centos (the X server of every run, a private display :99, 1280x1024x24, never the WSLg display), DejaVu fonts 2.33 and the misc and Type1 X fonts; compiler devtoolset-8 gcc/g++ 8.3.1 20190311 (Red Hat 8.3.1-3), cmake 3.23.3 (the image's own, no newer CMake was needed), Python 3.8 from /opt/python/cp38-cp38 for tools/build.py (the system Python of CentOS 6 is 2.6). The container runs on Docker Desktop 29.8.0 (engine linux/amd64) on the Windows 11 host of windows-11-x64 (WSL2 backend), so the KERNEL IS NOT CENTOS 6'S: it is the Microsoft WSL2 kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 shared with the host (uname -r in the container), on an Intel Core i5-8300H (x86_64). What this proves is the USERLAND floor: a binary built by that compiler against glibc 2.12 and its libraries loads and runs with them. What it does not prove: a real CentOS 6 kernel (2.6.32), a CentOS 6 boot, a real Xorg server, a window manager, a desktop or a real keyboard (the X server is Xvfb). Build and run happened inside the container; the worktree was mounted at /src and the build directory was a Docker volume mounted as /root/loomora-build, outside the repository. The yum repositories needed a workaround (vault.centos.org answered 403 Forbidden to the CentOS 6 TLS stack for the repodata files; see the Dockerfile).
eol_source: CentOS 6 reached end of life on 2020-11-30 (CentOS Project; its last release is 6.10, 2018-07-03, and its repositories moved to vault.centos.org). The Linux end-of-life test of the backend (loomora_is_eol) looks at the kernel release from uname, and the container reports the WSL2 kernel 6.18, which is not end of life: so eol_warning_shown is false in the probe lines of this platform although the distribution is end of life. The banner is not shown by this system (the kernel is the host's).
kernel: 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (uname -srm in the container: Linux 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64), the kernel of the Docker Desktop and WSL2 VM, not a CentOS 6 kernel (2.6.32)
compiler: gcc/g++ 8.3.1 20190311 (Red Hat 8.3.1-3), devtoolset-8-gcc-c++ 8.3.1-3.2.el6, with the devtoolset linker script that links the newer libstdc++ symbols statically; cmake 3.23.3, GNU make (no Ninja), Python 3.8 (/opt/python/cp38-cp38)
hardware: The host of windows-11-x64: MSI GL63 8RD, Intel Core i5-8300H (x86_64), 8 logical CPUs; the container has no CPU limit set
release_date_source: CentOS 6.10 release date 2018-07-03 (CentOS Project release announcement; the first CentOS 6 release is 6.0, 2011-07-10); age_years = days from 2018-07-03 to the trial date 2026-11-15 divided by 365.25. is_floor WAS true for the Linux Legacy UI (the lowest Linux system tried when it was written, owner's PoC rule); since the manylinux1 run it is false, see floor_note; the Linux Modern UI was not tried on it (verdict linux-centos-6.10-x86_64-modern, not_tested).
floor_note: Floor of the Linux Legacy UI for the PoC from 2026-11-15 until the manylinux1 run of the same day (the lowest testable Linux system then, the manylinux2010 container: CentOS 6.10 userland, glibc 2.12). NO LONGER THE FLOOR: it is superseded by linux-centos-5.11-x86_64 (manylinux1 container, CentOS 5.11 userland, glibc 2.5), a lower Linux userland that built and ran the same UI. Its verdict stays as it was: it is still a valid run on a higher system. The Linux Modern UI was not tried on it.
